secondary.title: Genghis Khan and the Making of the Modern World
secondary.author: Jack Weatherford
secondary.rationale: A widely acclaimed and influential scholarly work that provides a comprehensive overview of Genghis Khan's life, conquests, and lasting impact on global history. It is based on extensive research and is considered a standard text in the field.

secondary.title: The Secret History of the Mongols
secondary.author: Various (compiled by the Mongols)
secondary.rationale: While not authored by Genghis Khan himself, this is the most important contemporary source for his life and the early Mongol Empire. It is a foundational text for understanding the period and is available in numerous scholarly translations.

secondary.title: Genghis Khan: The Emperor of All Men
secondary.author: Harold Lamb
secondary.rationale: Although older, this biography by Harold Lamb remains a classic and highly readable account of Genghis Khan's life. It has been influential in shaping popular perceptions and continues to be referenced, though modern scholarship has updated some interpretations.

suggestions.notes: Direct primary sources authored by Genghis Khan are extremely rare and not readily available in digitized formats on common platforms like Wikisource or Project Gutenberg. His legacy is primarily understood through contemporary chronicles and later historical accounts.
